key_insight: A clustering-based wrapper feature selection method can match standard sequential selection performance while cutting computation for renewable energy prediction.
engineering_relevance: For wind and solar forecasting pipelines, CSFS offers a practical way to reduce sensor/input complexity without sacrificing prediction quality.
method: Compared CSFS with sequential feature selection, filter methods, and Random Forest feature importance.
Used structured literature reviews plus empirical evaluation on wind turbine power curve modeling and photovoltaic power prediction.
Relies on clustering to guide efficient, model-agnostic wrapper-based feature selection.
evidence_signal: Across both case studies, wrapper-based methods performed best overall, and CSFS achieved performance comparable to SFS with an average 21% reduction in computational cost.
watch_item: Results are based on two specific renewable-energy prediction settings, so transferability to other datasets, sensor configurations, or forecasting horizons should be validated.
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
